To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the epigenetic regulation of gene expression is modulated by adverse environmental conditions, such as stress.
stress imprinting and epigenetic regulation modulate the development and expression of complex disease phenotypes in subsequent generations and may represent a novel target of preventive medicine.
stress imprinting and epigenetic regulation represent a key determinant of health and diseases in the F3 and beyond.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the epigenetic mechanisms that underlie stress-induced transgenerational programming of gene expression.
epigenetic mechanisms and how they are affected by environmental stress and how this affects the health and well-being of the offspring.
the role of epigenetic mechanisms, particularly epigenetic memory formation, in stress imprinting, and transgenerational programming of complex disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
stress imprinting is an epigenetic phenomenon that is transgenerationally inherited, and that it can be reversed.
stress is an important environmental factor for the development of adult onset complex disease, and that stress imprinting and epigenetic memory are important factors in this process.
the epigenetic memory is a critical determinant of disease and health in the third and subsequent generations and may be of diagnostic and therapeutic relevance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
stress is not only a risk factor for adult-onset complex diseases but may also be an important determinant of the transgenerational origins for disease.
stress is a major determinant of health and well-being and can have transgenerational effects.
epigenetic memory is a key to understand the transgenerational transmission of disease risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the environment, particularly early in life and in utero, can have a profound impact on our health and disease risk.
epigenetic regulation represents an important mechanism of stress imprinting that can have long-term effects on health and disease.
the epigenetic landscape is not a fixed entity, but rather a dynamic system that is continuously shaped and remodeled by environmental factors.
